evals.prompt: Create a 5-slide PowerPoint pitch deck for Metis Strategy introducing our digital transformation practice to a new banking client. Include: (1) title slide, (2) the challenge banks face today, (3) Metis's approach, (4) key capabilities, (5) next steps. Make it look and feel on-brand for Metis.
evals.expected_output: A .pptx file using Metis brand colors (Dark Blue #20216f and Metis Green #3cdbc0 as primary anchors), Calibri font, proper slide structure, page numbers, confidentiality footer, and varied layouts across slides.

assertions.name: Uses correct primary brand colors
assertions.description: The generated PowerPoint uses Dark Blue (#20216f) and/or Metis Green (#3cdbc0) as primary accent colors — not generic blue, gray, or off-brand colors

assertions.name: Includes confidentiality footer
assertions.description: Slides include 'Proprietary & Confidential, Metis Strategy LLC' in the footer

assertions.name: Varied slide layouts
assertions.description: Slides use different layouts (not every slide is the same title + bullets pattern)

assertions.name: Tone is confident and insight-led
assertions.description: Slide titles and body copy lead with insights and recommendations, not just descriptive labels. Active voice used.

assertions.name: BrandLine appears on appropriate slide
assertions.description: The BrandLine 'Driving change. Elevating leaders.' appears on the title or closing slide

evals.prompt: Write a 2-page executive summary that Metis Strategy can send to a healthcare CEO summarizing initial AI readiness assessment findings. Key findings: (1) strong data infrastructure, (2) weak change management capability, (3) moderate AI talent pool. Include a recommended path forward. Make it on-brand for Metis.
evals.expected_output: A Word doc or equivalent with Dark Blue headers, proper Metis typography hierarchy, insight-led section headers (not just labels), BrandLine in footer, active confident voice, and a clear recommended path forward.

assertions.name: Section headers are declarative/insight-led
assertions.description: Headers state a finding or recommendation (e.g., 'Data Infrastructure Is a Competitive Advantage') rather than generic labels (e.g., 'Data Infrastructure')

assertions.name: Uses active voice and Metis tone
assertions.description: Document uses active voice, leads with insights, avoids filler phrases like 'it is worth noting that' or 'in order to'

assertions.name: Includes all three findings
assertions.description: Document addresses all three key findings: data infrastructure, change management, and AI talent

assertions.name: Includes a clear path forward / recommendations section
assertions.description: Document includes a recommended next steps or path forward section with actionable guidance

assertions.name: References brand colors or styling appropriately
assertions.description: If generating a document programmatically, uses Metis brand colors. If plain text/markdown, at minimum follows Metis tone and structure conventions.

evals.prompt: Draft a follow-up email from Metis partner Sarah Chen to John Martinez, CDO at a Fortune 100 retailer, after an initial discovery call. We discussed their inventory forecasting challenges and Metis's AI optimization capabilities. The email should recap the conversation, reinforce Metis's value, and propose a clear next step.
evals.expected_output: An email that sounds confident, direct, and senior-executive-appropriate. Leads with value, not process. Uses active voice. Avoids filler. Proposes a specific next step. Feels like it comes from a trusted strategic advisor, not a sales rep.

assertions.name: Leads with value or insight
assertions.description: Opening paragraph leads with a relevant insight or value statement, not a generic 'thank you for your time' opener

assertions.name: Proposes a specific next step
assertions.description: Email proposes a concrete, specific next step (e.g., 'I'd like to schedule a 30-minute working session' not just 'let's connect again')

assertions.name: Confident, direct tone — no hedging
assertions.description: Email uses Metis voice: confident, direct, no hedging phrases like 'we believe we might be able to' or 'potentially'

assertions.name: Appropriate length — not bloated
assertions.description: Email is appropriately concise for a senior executive — not overly long or padded with unnecessary pleasantries
